title: Patterns vs. Patients: Evaluating LLMs against Mental Health Professionals on Personality Disorder Diagnosis through First-Person Narratives

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing the categorical diagnostic accuracy and dimensional severity ratings of LLMs against clinical ground truth and human expert performance on first-person patient narratives, specifically measuring systematic overdiagnosis (e.g., Borderline Personality Disorder) and underdiagnosis (e.g., Narcissistic Personality Disorder).

Analyzing the distribution of assigned diagnostic labels to identify systematic tendencies of models to misclassify clinical cases as 'healthy' or avoid assigning stigmatizing, value-laden psychiatric terms (like 'narcissist'), linking this behavior to RLHF alignment and sycophancy.
